title.narrative: Reinforce the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions

description.narrative:
Namibia, as a State Party to the 2005 UNESCO Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions, is committed to promoting, raising awareness of, and effectively implementing the Convention. Since ratifying the Convention on 11 December 2006, Namibia has consistently submitted its Quadrennial Periodic Reports (QPRs), demonstrating sustained commitment to monitoring and reporting on implementation progress.
However, the convention requires civil society involvement to overcome issues related to policies and creative industry as a contributor to the country’s economic development. Support the implementation of a strategic objectives on strengthening the capacity, skills, and professionalisation of cultural and creative practitioners as part of the Action Plan derived from the Namibia Cultural and Creative Industries Strategy and activities aligned to the National Development Plan 6 (NDP 6). The proposed intervention will further complement ongoing efforts under the pilot project “Entrepreneurship for Sustainable Heritage Development of Local Communities in Namibia”, implemented within the broader UNESCO regional initiative “Creating a Sustainable Heritage Ecosystem for Socioeconomic Development in Africa.” Together, these initiatives aim to foster cultural entrepreneurship, stimulate inclusive economic growth, and improve livelihoods, particularly for communities linked to heritage resources. In parallel, the implementation of the UNESCO Culture|2030 Indicators will provide an evidence-based framework to assess and demonstrate the contribution of culture to the economic, social, and environmental dimensions of sustainable development. This data-driven approach will strengthen policy coherence, accountability, and advocacy for culture as a development enabler.
Therefore, ongoing awareness-raising activities will support structured public discussions and policy dialogues on the role of the cultural and creative industries as drivers of economic development, social cohesion, and social transformation. Within this framework, the annual celebration of International Jazz Day will serve as a strategic platform to highlight jazz as an educational tool and a powerful vehicle for intercultural dialogue, freedom of expression, and mutual understanding.
Key activities - Support activities related to the development and implementation of the Namibia Cultural and Creative Industries Strategy. - Provide support towards entrepreneurship for sustainable heritage development of local communities (through entrepreneurship training, hackathons across key creative industry subsectors). - Raise awareness through public discussions with the Ministry of Education, Innovation, Youth, Sports, Arts and Culture and partners to highlight cultural and creative industries as a driver for economic development. - Organize International Jazz Day celebrations, using the platform to promote intercultural dialogue, freedom of expression, and youth participation.
